sections.skill: Use federal and state consumer protections and file a complaint

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa's debit card is stolen. She reports it within 2 business days of noticing. Thieves spent $700. What is her most liability under federal rules?
questions.intro: Federal rules (Regulation E) limit debit card losses: $50 if you report within 2 business days of learning of the loss; up to $500 if later; and possibly unlimited if not reported within 60 days after the statement. Many banks offer more protection.
questions.feedback: Reported within 2 business days, her liability is at most $50.
questions.topic: Consumer rights and where to get help

misconceptions.C: Uses the limit for later reporting

sources: CFPB (Regulation E: lost or stolen debit cards): Liability for unauthorized debit card use is limited to $50 if reported within 2 business days of learning of the loss, up to $500 if reported later, and can be unlimited if not reported within 60 days after the statement is sent. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-do-i-get-my-money-back-after-a-debit-card-theft-en-1017/)

CFPB (Credit card fraud liability): Under federal law, liability for unauthorized credit card charges is at most $50. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-my-liability-for-unauthorized-credit-card-charges-en-24/)
CFPB (Submit a complaint): Consumers can submit complaints about financial products; the CFPB forwards them to companies for a response. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/complaint/)

FTC (Cooling-Off Rule): The Cooling-Off Rule gives buyers 3 days to cancel certain sales of $25 or more made at their home or at temporary locations. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/buyers-remorse-ftcs-cooling-rule-may-help)

New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs: New Jersey residents can file consumer complaints with the Division of Consumer Affairs, which enforces the New Jersey Consumer Fraud Act. (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/)

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: A debt collector calls Rosa at 2 a.m. and threatens jail. What is true?

choices.text: This breaks federal debt collection rules
Unpaid debts send people to jail
She must pay immediately to stop the calls

questions.correct_answer: This breaks federal debt collection rules
questions.intro: The Fair Debt Collection Practices Act bars collectors from harassment, threats, and calls before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. It also gives you the right to dispute a debt and get validation.
questions.feedback: Late-night calls and false threats violate the FDCPA.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa's credit card statement dated April 30 shows a $120 charge for an item never delivered. She mails a written dispute on June 15. Is it on time under the Fair Credit Billing Act?

choices.text: No; disputes must be made within 6 days of the purchase
No; disputes are allowed only before the item ships
Yes; it is within 60 days of the statement
Yes, because there is no deadline for billing errors

questions.correct_answer: Yes; it is within 60 days of the statement
questions.intro: The Fair Credit Billing Act lets you dispute billing errors, including goods not delivered, in writing within 60 days after the statement with the error was sent.
questions.feedback: April 30 to June 15 is 46 days, inside the 60-day window.

questions.feedback: Dispute within 30 days to require verification.
